extractions.quote: The above patient had most of the classical features of the stiff-man syndrome: onset in middle age; stiffness initially involving the trunk muscles with persistence of rigidity even at rest; superimposed painful spasms precipitated by stress and exertion; hyperlordosis of lumbar spine with restricted forward flexion; gradual progression over months; otherwise normal neurological examination with normal higher functions, motor power, sensations and reflexes; characteristic EMG changes of continuous normal motor unit activity at rest in affected muscles with no signs of denervation or primary muscle disease and normal nerve conduction studies.

Extrapyramidal syndromes like torsion dystonias, progressive encephalomyelitis, spinal cord lesions, localized tetanus, Issac's syndrome and myotonia can closely mimic the stiff-man syndrome. These and other local pathologies like peritonitis can be differentiated by the classical features of the disease together with electrophysiological studies
